full_judgment: 2. The petitioner as plaintiff filed a suit being Title Suit No. 63 of 1999 on 10-11-1999 under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act in the Court of Assistant Judge, Rajapur, against the defendant-opposite parties praying for a decree of recovery of possession of the Kha schedule land contending, inter alia, that Ananta Kumar, Madhusudhan and Rahini Kumar were owners and possessors of 1.30 acres of land of SA Khatian No. 1354, Plot No. 4103 of Mouza Rajapur, PS Rajapur, district Jhalakati, and that Madhusudan died leaving his cousin Ananta Kumar as his heir, that Ananta Kumar sold 0.21 decimals of land to the plaintiff petitioner vide registered deed No. 4209 dated 25-11-1969 and delivered possession of the said land from the northeastern portion of plot No. 4103, and that the plaintiff petitioner mutated his name and paid rents and has been possessing the same, that the plaintiff dug out a pond from the western portion of the land and filled earth and created a passage from the eastern portion to flow water and made east facing road and planted different, kinds of trees, constructed tinshed house with wire surrounding for more than 30 years. It was further contended that Rajapur Pilot High School has no right, title, interest and possession on the suit land and the defendant-opposite party Nos. 2-4 teachers of the said school used to reside towards the southern Plot No. 4099 of Plot No. 4103. But the defendant-opposite party No. 1, headmaster of the said school, for the benefit and advantage of defendant opposite party Nos. 2-4 by using the name of Rajapur Pilot High School illegally threatened to grab the Suit land, the plaintiff-petitioner filed Miscellaneous Petition Case No. 263 of 1999 in the Court of learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Jhalakati, and that during pendency of the said case, the threat was continued and on 15-4-1999 GD Entry No. 514 was made with the Rajapur, Police Station. Thereafter, on 17-4-1999 under the leadership of the defendant -opposite party No.1 along with other defendant opposite parties forcibly dispossessed the plaintiff petitioner from the 0.8 decimals of land described in the schedule 'kha' of the plaint. The defendant opposite party No. 1 in order to legalise his illegal activities of dispossession of the plaintiff petitioner from the suit land made a statement in the Daily Ajker Barta dated 18-4-1999 and thereafter, under the leadership of defendant opposite party No. 1 some hired people broke an old tin shed adjacent to the main building of the school and reconstructed the said tin shed on the eastern portion of the land of the plaintiff petitioner and created obstacle to the access of the house of him. Thereafter, the defendant opposite party No. 1 cut earth from the southeast portion of the suit plot and filled up the floor of the newly constructed tin shed and changed the nature and character of the land of the plaintiff petitioner. Thereafter, on 12-5-1999 while the defendant opposite parties started unfinished work of the newly constructed tin shed, the plaintiff petitioner informed the matter to the police of Rajapur Police Station and the police issued warning notice but the defendant opposite parties completed the unfinished work disobeying the warning notice. The defendant opposite parties having no right, title, interest and possession of the suit land and being completely strangers, caused damage to the plaintiff petitioner amounting to Taka 50,000 by dispossessing him from the suit land and changing the nature and character of it. The plaintiff petitioner requested the defendant opposite parties to hand over the possession of the suit land after removing the tin shed structure but the defendant opposite parties refused and, as such, the suit under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act was filed.
